question: A pull-request review agent is meant to flag branches (conditional paths) that lack test coverage. In practice it inconsistently flags newly introduced branches that are already exercised indirectly by an existing integration test, producing noisy false positives that erode reviewer trust. Detailed instructions about 'coverage' have not resolved the inconsistency. What should the team add to the prompt?
options: A) A couple of examples pairing a diff with a coverage judgment: one branch with no test, one covered indirectly
B) A rule treating any file changed by fewer than ten lines as automatically having adequate coverage
C) A requirement to run the full test suite and flag any branch under one hundred percent line coverage
D) An instruction to flag every new conditional branch in a diff regardless of the surrounding test suite entirely
correct_answers: A) A couple of examples pairing a diff with a coverage judgment: one branch with no test, one covered indirectly
explanations: Correct. Showing a genuinely uncovered branch alongside a lookalike branch that is indirectly covered, with the resulting judgment for each, demonstrates the exact distinction the agent needs to generalize, which is the ambiguous-case handling that few-shot examples are designed to convey.

An arbitrary line-count threshold is unrelated to whether a branch actually has test coverage and would let genuinely uncovered small diffs slip through while ignoring the indirect-coverage ambiguity entirely.

Running the full suite and enforcing a strict coverage percentage swaps in a numeric gate instead of resolving the ambiguous case the prompt is failing on, and it does not use examples to teach the distinction.

Flagging every new branch unconditionally removes the judgment call entirely and guarantees the same false-positive pattern the team is trying to eliminate, since indirectly covered branches would still be flagged.
